Baseboard & Trim Calculator

Baseboard calculator: room perimeter minus doorways to linear feet of trim and number of 8, 12 or 16 ft pieces.

How to measure baseboard

Measure every wall where baseboard runs, add them up, and subtract door openings (about 3 ft for a standard interior door). Add 10–15% for miter and cope cuts—every inside or outside corner consumes a little extra.

Example: 48 ft perimeter − 3 ft door = 45 ft. Plus 10% = 49.5 ft ÷ 12 = 4.1 → 5 pieces of 12 ft.

Buying tips

  • Longer pieces (16 ft) mean fewer scarf joints on long walls.
  • Use the same calculation for crown molding (measure the ceiling perimeter) and shoe molding.
  • Prefinished MDF is cheapest for painted trim; use PVC in damp basements and bathrooms.
